audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is root() computation deterministic across calls?

code_scope.lines: N/A - Trie root computation is implementation-wide

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Root computation uses Keccak256 hash of serialized trie nodes. Determinism depends on consistent node serialization order.
potential_issues: Dictionary iteration order in older .NET versions could cause non-determinism, but modern .NET uses stable ordering for Dictionary<K,V>

phase2_semantic_validation.specification_reference: Ethereum Yellow Paper - World State Trie
invariants_checked: Same trie state produces same root hash

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Nethermind's PatriciaTree implementation uses deterministic Keccak256 hashing and consistent node serialization. Modern .NET dictionaries maintain insertion order. The implementation has been battle-tested across mainnet consensus.
phase3_formal_classification.recommended_action: No immediate action required. Continue monitoring cross-client consensus tests.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does insert-then-delete restore original trie state?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Setting a key to default value (null/empty) triggers deletion. Trie structure collapses back to original form if no other keys affected.
potential_issues: Edge case where branch node doesn't collapse properly after deletion

invariants_checked: insert(k,v) then delete(k) restores original root

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Nethermind's trie implementation properly handles node collapse after deletion. Existing test coverage in TrieTests.cs validates insert-delete cycles.
phase3_formal_classification.recommended_action: Ensure comprehensive test coverage for SELFDESTRUCT and storage zeroing edge cases.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is common_prefix_length computation bounded by O(N*L)?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Common prefix computation is O(L) per key where L is key length. Total complexity is O(N*L) for N keys.
potential_issues: No explicit timeout mechanism for pathological inputs

assumptions_validated: Key length is bounded (32 bytes for addresses)

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Algorithmic complexity is bounded by design. Key length is fixed at 32 bytes (64 nibbles). However, block gas limits and EIP-7825 transaction gas caps provide additional protection.
phase3_formal_classification.recommended_action: Consider adding explicit processing time limits for block validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is state sync memory consumption bounded?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: State sync processes nodes iteratively with bounded memory pools.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: State sync implementation was not fully analyzed. Memory bounds depend on configuration and batch processing limits.
phase3_formal_classification.attack_scenario: Attacker sends deeply nested branch nodes causing stack overflow or memory exhaustion
phase3_formal_classification.recommended_action: Audit state sync memory management and add explicit depth limits if not present.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are all Fusaka types handled explicitly in encode_node?

potential_issues: New Fusaka/Osaka types may not be handled

invariants_checked: All types have explicit encoding path

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Fusaka-specific encoding changes require detailed review against specification. This is a consensus-critical area.
phase3_formal_classification.attack_scenario: New type falls through to wrong encoding path causing consensus split
phase3_formal_classification.recommended_action: Review encode_node implementation against Osaka/Fusaka specification. Add exhaustive type checks.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is type-safe equality used in trie_set default comparison?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: C# uses type-safe equality by default. Byte array comparisons use SequenceEqual or span comparison.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: C# is a strongly-typed language. Unlike Python, there's no implicit type coercion in equality comparisons. byte[] comparison is explicit.
phase3_formal_classification.recommended_action: No action required. C# type system provides protection.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does encode_node produce non-empty output for all valid values?

assumptions_validated: RLP encoder handles all valid inputs

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: RLP encoding specification ensures minimum output size. However, specific validation would require code inspection.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transaction gasLimit > 16777216 rejected at txpool admission?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: GasLimitCapTxValidator is registered for ALL transaction types (Legacy, AccessList, EIP1559, Blob, SetCode). Validation occurs via CompositeTxValidator chain.

assumptions_validated: GasLimitCapTxValidator is in all tx type validator chains

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Implementation correctly uses strict greater-than comparison (>) against cap. Validation is applied to ALL transaction types via GasLimitCapTxValidator in TxValidator constructor. Test coverage exists in TxPoolTests.cs and TxValidatorTests.cs.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is GAS_CAP constant exactly 16777216 (2^24)?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Constant is defined as 16_777_216 which equals 2^24 = 16777216. Used by GetTxGasLimitCap when EIP-7825 is enabled.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Constant is correctly defined as 16_777_216 (2^24 = 16777216). It's declared as static readonly ensuring immutability.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is tx gas cap independent from block gas limit?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: GetTxGasLimitCap takes only IReleaseSpec as parameter, not block gas limit. Returns fixed constant 16777216 when EIP-7825 enabled.
potential_issues: None - cap is independent of block gas limit

assumptions_validated: No block gas limit parameter in cap calculation

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: The tx gas cap is a protocol constant that does not reference block gas limit. GetTxGasLimitCap only checks IsEip7825Enabled flag.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation iterate ALL transactions for gas cap check?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Block validation iterates all transactions. Each transaction validated by TxValidator which includes GasLimitCapTxValidator.
potential_issues: Early exit on first error (but this is correct behavior)

invariants_checked: Block rejected if ANY tx invalid
assumptions_validated: Validation iterates full list or stops on first error
edge_cases_considered: Invalid tx at position N/2, position N

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Block validation processes all transactions. Early exit on first error is acceptable since block is rejected anyway.
phase3_formal_classification.recommended_action: Verify block validation uses TxValidator for all transactions.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is entire block rejected if ANY transaction exceeds gas cap?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: TxValidator returns ValidationResult.Failure on invalid tx. Block validation fails the entire block.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Ethereum block validation is atomic - any invalid transaction invalidates the entire block.

invariants_checked: All executed txs have gasLimit <= cap

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: GasLimitCapTxValidator enforces cap before transaction can be included in valid block.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: GasLimitCapTxValidator is registered for all tx types in TxValidator constructor. TxValidator is used by both txpool and block validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is cap value 16777216 identical at txpool and block validation?

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Single constant in Eip7825Constants used everywhere. No duplication or hardcoded values found.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is multiplication_complexity >= 16 for all ModExp inputs?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: When EIP-7883 enabled: returns 16 for small inputs (max <= 32), or 2*words^2 for large inputs (which is always >= 18 for max=33).

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: MultComplexity explicitly returns 16UL as floor when max <= 32. For max > 32, minimum is 2*5^2=50. Complexity is always >= 16.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is multiplication_complexity exactly 16 when max(base_length, modulus_length) <= 32?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Code: if (isEip7883Enabled) { return max > LengthSize ? (sq << 1) : 16UL; } where LengthSize = 32.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Code explicitly returns 16UL when max <= LengthSize (32) and isEip7883Enabled is true.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is multiplication_complexity = 2*ceil(max_length/8)^2 for large operands?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: words = ceil(max/8) via (max+7)/8. sq = words^2. Result = sq << 1 = 2*words^2.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Implementation matches EIP-7883 specification exactly: 2*ceil(max_length/8)^2.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is iteration_count >= 1 for all non-trivial ModExp inputs?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: For small exponents: Math.Max(1, ...). For large exponents: explicit check iterationCount < 1.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Code explicitly enforces minimum of 1 in both small and large exponent paths via Math.Max and explicit check.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is iteration_count exactly 1 for zero exponent with length <= 32?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: For exponent=0, BitLen=0, so Math.Max(1, 0-1) = Math.Max(1, -1) = 1.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: For zero exponent, BitLen=0, so exponent.BitLen-1=-1, and Math.Max(1,-1)=1. Returns exactly 1.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is large exponent multiplier 16 (not 8) in iteration_count formula?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Multiplier is 16 when isEip7883Enabled=true, 8 otherwise.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: IterationCountMultiplierEip7883 is explicitly defined as 16 and used when isEip7883Enabled is true.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is ModExp gas cost >= 500 for all inputs?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Math.Max enforces minimum of GasCostOf.MinModExpEip7883 (500) when EIP-7883 enabled.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Code uses Math.Max to enforce minimum gas cost of 500 (GasCostOf.MinModExpEip7883) when EIP-7883 is enabled.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does ModExp gas formula NOT include /3 divisor?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: Division by 3 is ONLY applied when EIP-7883 is NOT enabled. When EIP-7883 is enabled, no division.

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Code explicitly only divides by 3 when EIP-7883 is NOT enabled: if (!releaseSpec.IsEip7883Enabled) { result /= 3; }

audit_items.title: Verify Boundary Condition: Does txpool use strict comparison (> not >=) for gas cap?

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Code uses > operator: transaction.GasLimit > gasLimitCap. This means 16777216 is accepted, 16777217 rejected.

audit_items.title: Verify Post-Condition: Is multiplication_complexity = 2*ceil(max_length/8)^2 when max_length > 32?

phase1_structural_analysis.data_flow_analysis: words = (max + 7) >> 3 = ceil(max/8). sq = words^2. Returns sq << 1 = 2*sq when max > 32.

audit_items.title: Verify Post-Condition: Is iteration_count using multiplier 16 for exponent_length > 32?

phase3_formal_classification.rationale: Code uses IterationCountMultiplierEip7883 (16) when EIP-7883 enabled and exponent_length > 32.
